title: Returned Payments on Operating Lines of Credit — Reversal, Fee and AutoDraft Cancellation
content:
When the member's bank returns a payment on one of the Operating Lines of Credit unpaid, exactly that payment is reversed.

## Rules

1. **Reversal.** The return entry carries the original payment's amount and effective date and points to that payment, so balances and interest are restated as though the payment had never been made. The reversal is back-dated to the original payment's effective date.
2. **Once only.** A payment may be reversed only once.
3. **Returned payment fee.** Unless the return reason is that the debit was unauthorized, a returned payment fee of the product's returned payment fee amount is assessed, pointing to the return entry. A debit the member did not authorise carries no fee.
4. **AutoDraft cancellation.** When a second AutoDraft payment on the line is returned within the rolling window — that is, when the count of returned AutoDraft payments reaches 2 — AutoDraft is cancelled the day the second return is booked, which removes the AutoDraft discount from the contract rate.

The rolling window for the count is the 12 months ending on the date considered, running from the same calendar date one year earlier (exclusive) through that date (inclusive). Only returns whose original payment was collected by AutoDraft are counted.

## Fee table

| Return reason | Payment reversed | Returned payment fee |
|---|---|---|
| Any reason other than unauthorized | Yes | Yes |
| Unauthorized | Yes | No |

## Count of returned AutoDraft payments (hypothetical, return booked on 10 June)

| AutoDraft returns already in the window ending 10 June | Effect of the 10 June return |
|---|---|
| None | First return in the window; the count is 1 and has not reached 2 |
| One, on 20 September of the previous year | Second return in the window (2); AutoDraft is cancelled on 10 June |
| One, on 10 June of the previous year | That date is outside the window (exclusive); the 10 June return is the first in the window, and the count of 1 has not reached 2 |
